pr_body:
`fs.rename` doesn't work across partitions, so we have to have
tmp folder next to our final destination.

Fixes #2494

issue_context.title: [REGRESSION]: Atomic binary install failing in CI
issue_context.body:
**Context:**
- GOOD Playwright Version: before https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/2489
- BAD Playwright Version: after https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/2489
- Operating System: Linux
- Extra: Jenkins with Docker

**Code Snippet**

```sh
npm i playwright-chromium@1.1.0-next.1591502446737
```

**Describe the bug**

Hey team. The atomic install change is causing some issues for me in Docker on Jenkins. Here's what I get when I try to install.

```sh
(node:63) UnhandledPromiseRejectionWarning: Error: EXDEV: cross-device link not permitted, rename '/tmp/playwright-extract-chromium-linux-775089-9VigpJ' -> '/var/lib/jenkins/workspace/my-job/test/e2e/node_modules/playwright-chromium/.local-browsers/chromium-775089'
(node:63) UnhandledPromiseRejectionWarning: Unhandled promise rejection. This error originated either by throwing inside of an async function without a catch block, or by rejecting a promise which was not handled with .catch(). To terminate the node process on unhandled promise rejection, use the CLI flag `--unhandled-rejections=strict` (see https://nodejs.org/api/cli.html#cli_unhandled_rejections_mode). (rejection id: 1)
(node:63) [DEP0018] DeprecationWarning: Unhandled promise rejections are deprecated. In the future, promise rejections that are not handled will terminate the Node.js process with a non-zero exit code.
```

My understanding is that this means the tmp dir and the NPM install dir are on different partitions. I don't know if this is an edge case or something that the majority of Jenkins/Docker users will experience, but I wanted to raise it here in case you think it's worth addressing.

review_comments: Would it make sense to add a unique suffix to the file name to avoid possible conflicts e.g. when there are two playwrights are trying to install in parallel and when the previous download failed for some reason?
we explicitly do not support concurrent access to this folder - it would require lockdirs with pid files and all the fun. We'd rather stay away from this world for now.
Does this work to remove zip files?
